1.w: Now on the first day of the week, at early dawn, the women went to the tomb, taking the aromatic spices they had prepared.

2.w: They found that the stone had been rolled away from the tomb,

3.w: but when they went in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

4.w: While they were perplexed about this, suddenly two men stood beside them in dazzling attire.

5.w: The women were terribly frightened and bowed their faces to the ground, but the men said to them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead?

6.w: He is not here, but has been raised! Remember how he told you, while he was still in Galilee,

7.w: that the Son of Man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.”

8.w: Then the women remembered his words,

9.w: and when they returned from the tomb, they told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.

10.w: Now it was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the other women with them who told these things to the apostles.

11.w: But these words seemed like pure nonsense to them, and they did not believe them.

12.w: But Peter got up and ran to the tomb. He bent down and saw only the strips of linen cloth; then he went home, wondering what had happened.

13.w: Now that very day two of them were on their way to a village called Emmaus, about seven miles from Jerusalem.

14.w: They were talking to each other about all the things that had happened.

15.w: While they were talking and debating these things, Jesus himself approached and began to accompany them

16.w: (but their eyes were kept from recognizing him).

17.w: Then he said to them, “What are these matters you are discussing so intently as you walk along?” And they stood still, looking sad.

18.w: Then one of them, named Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who doesn’t know the things that have happened there in these days?”

19.w: He said to them, “What things?” “The things concerning Jesus the Nazarene,” they replied, “a man who, with his powerful deeds and words, proved to be a prophet before God and all the people;

20.w: and how our chief priests and leaders handed him over to be condemned to death, and crucified him.

21.w: But we had hoped that he was the one who was going to redeem Israel. Not only this, but it is now the third day since these things happened.

22.w: Furthermore, some women of our group amazed us. They were at the tomb early this morning,

23.w: and when they did not find his body, they came back and said they had seen a vision of angels, who said he was alive.

24.w: Then some of those who were with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”

25.w: So he said to them, “You foolish people —how slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!

26.w: Wasn’t it necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and enter into his glory?”

27.w: Then beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he interpreted to them the things written about himself in all the scriptures.

28.w: So they approached the village where they were going. He acted as though he wanted to go farther,

29.w: but they urged him, “Stay with us because it is getting toward evening and the day is almost done.” So he went in to stay with them.

30.w: When he had taken his place at the table with them, he took the bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them.

31.w: At this point their eyes were opened and they recognized him. Then he vanished out of their sight.

32.w: They said to each other, “Didn’t our hearts burn within us while he was speaking with us on the road, while he was explaining the scriptures to us?”

33.w: So they got up that very hour and returned to Jerusalem. They found the eleven and those with them gathered together

34.w: and saying, “The Lord has really risen and has appeared to Simon!”

35.w: Then they told what had happened on the road, and how they recognized him when he broke the bread.

36.w: While they were saying these things, Jesus himself stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”

37.w: But they were startled and terrified, thinking they saw a ghost.

38.w: Then he said to them, “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?

39.w: Look at my hands and my feet; it’s me! Touch me and see; a ghost does not have flesh and bones like you see I have.”

40.w: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his feet.

41.w: And while they still could not believe it (because of their joy) and were amazed, he said to them, “Do you have anything here to eat?”

42.w: So they gave him a piece of broiled fish,

43.w: and he took it and ate it in front of them.

44.w: Then he said to them, “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you, that everything written about me in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms must be fulfilled.”

45.w: Then he opened their minds so they could understand the scriptures,

46.w: and said to them, “Thus it stands written that the Christ would suffer and would rise from the dead on the third day,

47.w: and repentance for the forgiveness of sins would be proclaimed in his name to all nations, beginning from Jerusalem.

48.w: You are witnesses of these things.

49.w: And look, I am sending you what my Father promised. But stay in the city until you have been clothed with power from on high.”

50.w: Then Jesus led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands, he blessed them.

51.w: Now during the blessing he departed and was taken up into heaven.

52.w: So they worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy,

53.w: and were continually in the temple courts blessing God.
